body_en:
This article is reposted from a post by the respected former President Joe Biden, published on X on November 9, 2026. Original post: https://x.com/joebiden/status/2119566187986120705

I want to share a brief update.

My presidential memoir, PROMISE ME, AMERICA, is coming out on November 17th. I hope you'll read it. It covers my years as President — the challenges we faced, the decisions I made, and why I made them. It's about who we are as a nation, what we stand for, and America's role in the world. More than anything, it's about my faith in the American people, and in the great American experiment in self-governance and democracy.

While writing the book, I was diagnosed with cancer — a disease known all too well to millions of Americans and their families. My doctors continue to be encouraged by how I've responded to treatment. And the prayers, the kind words, and the well wishes from so many of you have meant more to me, to Jill, and to our family than you could ever know.

Some days are better than others. It hasn't stopped me. But sometimes it slows me down. That means, unfortunately, I won't be able to do as many conversations about my book as I'd hoped. But I believe the words on the page will speak for themselves.

Looking forward, I'll keep following what my father told me a long time ago: "Champ, when you get knocked down, get up." It's a good lesson for me. And for America.

We are blessed. America is the most unique nation on earth. Unlike other countries, we're built on an idea — an idea bigger than any ocean, more powerful than any army, stronger than any tyrant or dictator. What is that idea? That all of us are created equal.

Promise Me, America — we'll never forget it.

excerpt_en: Former President Joe Biden announces his memoir, PROMISE ME, AMERICA, out November 17 — and shares, with striking candor, that he was diagnosed with cancer while writing it.
